state.request: Replace the redundant multi-command UX with a single Empirical entrypoint installed for every detected supported agent. Keep only empirical install and empirical update as normal human terminal lifecycle commands; the installed agent entrypoint must initialize an uninitialized repository, create and maintain compact repository knowledge, conduct Socratic discovery only when needed, choose Fast or Complex internally, resume active work, and after an approved spec offer to continue in the current agent, save, or launch a user-selected detected agent. Preserve structured MCP operations as internal automation APIs and hidden compatibility surfaces where necessary, remove separate Explore, Fast, Complex, and Loop installed skills from the normal user experience, never launch an agent without explicit approval, and verify lifecycle installation/update, agent-owned initialization, repository knowledge refresh, routing, resume, agent detection, explicit handoff, and worktree startup from repositories containing terminal or blocked historical feature state.

evidence.summary: Isolated-home integration and CLI tests proved install works outside a repository, creates one entrypoint for each selected agent, reports invocation/reload metadata, and creates no project state.
Migration fixtures removed marker-owned legacy skills while preserving unmanaged files, non-files, symbolic-link targets, and content outside the selected home.
Lifecycle runner tests verified npm global update occurs before the new empirical install process and package versus integration failures remain stage-specific.
Source and bundled CLI tests verified primary help exposes install/update only, README documents the one in-agent entrypoint, and MCP smoke retained all typed internal workflow operations.

Initialization fixtures verified safe configuration, runtime MCP bridges, repository context creation, and zero project-local workflow entrypoints; the generated skill carries material first-run configuration fields.

Knowledge tests verified deterministic byte-stable manifests, overview/architecture/commands/conventions pages, refresh on source change, topic preservation, secret exclusions, digest-only inventory, and packet context paths.

The installed-skill contract and integration tests verified initialization, context, resume-first behavior, five Socratic passes for ambiguity, strict Fast eligibility, Complex fallback, and no separate installed workflow skills.
Core handoff tests rejected pre-Specify use and verified the post-Specify offer contains current, save, and detected-agent choices without starting a process.

Agent fixtures distinguished prompt and workspace capabilities, asserted exact cwd/argv/prompt fields, required explicit approval, authorized unchanged tokens, rejected stale spec-bound tokens, and observed no launch side effect.

Real Git tests proved a linked worktree starts its intended feature when the committed base contains a blocked feature owned by the source checkout, while the source remains resumable and checkout claims do not collide.
Repeated install, initialization, knowledge refresh, schema migration, discovery, unmanaged-content, whitespace-preservation, symlink, and non-Git-to-Git fixtures all converged safely.

bun run ci passed: TypeScript check, 68 tests with 395 expectations, built CLI/MCP smoke including context and handoff, and npm dry-run for empirical-sdd@0.20.0 with 21 packaged files; git diff --check also passed.

Reviewed the complete source, tests, generated skill, docs, package output, and removals against AC-1 through AC-12 and accepted decisions D-001 through D-005. One review gap—lazy rather than immediate Done selection cleanup—was corrected transactionally and covered with recovery, release, and ambiguity tests. No blocking correctness, security, compatibility, or decision-alignment findings remain; unmanaged content and symlink boundaries are preserved, handoff never launches directly, internal APIs remain available, and publication remains out of scope.
